thesis: ASML Holding — monopoly supplier of EUV lithography systems, the chokepoint enabling every advanced semiconductor node. Structural beneficiary of the AI-driven chip capex supercycle regardless of which chipmaker wins. Inherited from 2026-06-03 session (replaced NVDA in Tech sleeve). Risk: China export controls, lumpy order timing. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Technology.

Microsoft — Azure cloud + Copilot AI monetization on top of an entrenched enterprise software franchise and durable recurring revenue. Inherited from 2026-06-03 session (replaced DDOG in Tech sleeve). Less exposed to the GPU-vs-ASIC chip rotation than hardware names. Risk: AI capex digestion, cloud growth deceleration. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Technology.

AbbVie — large-cap pharma with Skyrizi/Rinvoq immunology growth engines now well past the Humira patent cliff, plus a deep aesthetics and neuroscience portfolio and a ~3% dividend. Inherited from 2026-06-03 session (replaced MDGL in Healthcare sleeve; lower-volatility quality vs single-drug biotech). Risk: pipeline setbacks, drug-pricing policy. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Healthcare.

Eli Lilly — best-in-class GLP-1/obesity and diabetes franchise (tirzepatide) with a deep, durable pipeline. Buy consensus, avg PT ~$1,215-1,265; up ~5.6% since entry. Second Healthcare slot alongside ABBV. Risk: GLP-1 competition, pricing pressure, high valuation. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Healthcare.

JPMorgan Chase — best-in-class money-center bank; Q1 FY26 revenue +10% YoY, NII +9%, results beat. Buy consensus, median PT ~$345. Up ~3.7% since entry. Second Financials slot alongside V. Risk: rate/regulatory headwinds, credit cycle. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Financials.
Visa — global payments network with a durable toll-booth moat and secular tailwind from the shift to digital/cashless payments. Roughly flat since entry; thesis intact. Sector: Financials.

Costco — high-quality compounder; Q3 FY26 net sales +11.6%, comps +9.8%, digital comps +21.5%, membership fee income +10.7%. Up ~3.4% since entry. First Consumer Staples slot. Risk: rich P/E leaves little margin for a growth stumble. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Consumer Staples.

Procter & Gamble — defensive consumer-staples compounder with a portfolio of category-leading daily-use brands, pricing power, and a Dividend King track record. Inherited from 2026-06-02 session as the second Consumer Staples slot alongside COST (lower-beta ballast). Risk: volume softness, FX, input-cost inflation. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Consumer Staples.

Occidental Petroleum — Berkshire-backed energy major; oil structurally supported but a live geopolitical binary. Up ~4.6% since entry. Energy sector ballast. Risk: a US-Iran deal / Middle East de-escalation could soften crude (oil declining on Israel-Lebanon ceasefire). Sole Energy slot. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Energy.

McDonald's — defensive, franchise-heavy global QSR with durable brand, pricing power, and a reliable dividend; value menu wins share in a cautious consumer environment. Inherited from 2026-06-02 session; now the sole Consumer Discretionary slot after AMZN was stopped out 2026-06-03. Roughly flat since entry. Risk: traffic softness, FX. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Consumer Discretionary.

Vanguard Total International Stock ETF — broad developed + emerging markets ex-US in one low-cost fund (ER ~0.05%). Geographic diversification anchor. Roughly flat since entry. Tailwinds: weak USD, international equities outperforming US YTD. Risk: USD strength reversal, EM/geopolitical volatility. First International slot. Hold weeks-months. Sector: International/Diversified.

Alphabet — Search/YouTube/Cloud franchise with a Strong Buy consensus. A key winner in the GPU-to-custom-silicon (ASIC) shift that hit Broadcom: its TPUs gain as OpenAI/Anthropic scale compute faster than expected. Waymo robotaxi optionality strengthening as Tesla's driverless fleet shrinks. Initiates the Communication Services sector (was 0). Risk: ad-cycle sensitivity, AI-search disruption to core, antitrust. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Communication Services.

Caterpillar — global heavy-machinery leader and the single largest contributor to the Industrials sector's +16% YTD run. New tailwind: its generators help power AI data centers and an expanded Nvidia collaboration brings physical AI/robotics to heavy industry. Initiates the Industrials sector (was 0). Risk: cyclical construction/mining demand, not viewed as undervalued. Hold weeks-months. Sector: Industrials.
